t: You're looking at St Ermin's Hotel, a Grade II listed late Victorian building beside St James's Park Underground station. It was built as one of the early mansion blocks in the capital and converted to a hotel between 1896 and 1899. The site is thought to be named after an ancient monastery. From the 1930s it became a haunt of the British intelligence services, and it was the birthplace of the Special Operations Executive. The architect was Edwin Thomas Hall, who is also known for the Liberty department store and the Old Library at Dulwich College.
